findings.title: Retry counter is a read-modify-write on a stale value
findings.body: `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` writes a value computed from the row read at the start of the run. If two cron invocations overlap (or a manual call runs alongside the cron), both read the same count and both write count+1, so a failure is lost and the reminder takes longer to reach the deletion threshold. Prisma supports an atomic `retryCount: { increment: 1 }`, which avoids this. The same pattern is used in the catch block at line 195.

findings.title: Unguarded update in catch block can abort the whole cron loop
findings.body: The `prisma.workflowReminder.update` in the catch block (line 190) sits outside any try. If it throws (for example the reminder was deleted by the preceding deleteMany or by a concurrent request, which makes Prisma raise P2025), the exception propagates out of the `for` loop. Every remaining unscheduled reminder in that run is then skipped and the handler returns an error. One bad row can stall the whole batch on each cron run. The update should be wrapped in its own try/catch, or use `updateMany`, which does not throw when no row matches.

findings.title: Failure after a successful Twilio schedule increments retry and can cause duplicate SMS
findings.body: If `twilio.scheduleSMS` succeeds but the following `prisma.workflowReminder.update` (setting scheduled/referenceId, line 169) throws, control goes to the catch block. That block increments retryCount and leaves `scheduled` false. On the next run the same reminder is scheduled with Twilio again, so the attendee can receive the same SMS twice. The retry counter now makes this path more visible. The success-side update and the failure bookkeeping should not be conflated, or the reminder should be checked for an existing referenceId before rescheduling.

findings.title: retryCount deletion clause is not scoped to SMS or to unscheduled reminders
findings.body: The new `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` branch of the OR matches any WorkflowReminder regardless of `method` or `scheduled`. Only the SMS path increments retryCount today, so the effect is currently limited. But a future email or WhatsApp retry path would have its reminders deleted by this SMS-cleanup job. Adding `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` and `scheduled: false` to that branch would make the intent explicit and safe.

findings.title: Comment describes only the date-based deletion
findings.body: The comment on line 28 says the job deletes SMS reminders whose scheduled date has passed. The deleteMany now also deletes reminders after two failed attempts (`retryCount > 1`), which is the behaviour the PR is about. The comment is now misleading. The magic threshold `1` is also duplicated in no named constant, so its meaning ('deleted after the second failure') is not documented anywhere.

findings.title: No tests for the new retry and deletion behaviour
findings.body: The PR changes retry bookkeeping, the deletion threshold and the error path, but adds no unit or integration tests. Nothing verifies that a reminder is deleted after exactly two failures, that a successful schedule does not increment the counter, or that the catch path behaves correctly. The existing handler has no test coverage here, so regressions in this logic would go unnoticed.
